findings.desc: [codex-host-2, verified] gold-edit[refreshed] is mislabeled benign. The frozen candidate only adds an ignored top-level field; but a SEMANTIC gold edit (weaken a gold query's expectedIds/mustNotSurfaceIds, keep query IDs present, refresh goldDigest) yields status:pass (empirically confirmed: dropping one expectedId from the host-policy query -> pass). The instrument computes expected/must-not metrics from the (mutated) gold file itself, so refreshed oracle-weakening is an undetected tamper. The matrix must enumerate a malicious gold-semantic-weaken[refreshed] class and disposition it as an acknowledged instrument blind spot (Tier-C, per claim boundary), NOT conflate the gold-refresh axis with benign row-order tolerance.

[codex-host-2, verified] Refreshed corruptRows manifest lie is missing and passes. Setting manifest.corruptRows 1->0 and recomputing manifestDigest (records/gold unchanged) yields status:pass with malformedRowsSkipped=1 (empirically confirmed) — the verifier never cross-checks malformedRowsSkipped against manifest.corruptRows. The current disposition rule would mis-classify this as 'dropped' (records/gold byte-identical) though the manifest is lying. Enumerate corruptRows-lie[refreshed] and disposition as acknowledged blind spot.
